preamble.summary: Chapter 14 is the golden age of Simon's rule. It opens with Demetrius II's capture by the Parthians, then presents a magnificent praise poem for Simon's reign of peace and prosperity. The Spartans and Romans confirm their alliances. The chapter culminates in the great decree of the Jewish people (vv. 27-49) formally conferring on Simon and his descendants the offices of high priest, commander, and ethnarch — creating the Hasmonean dynasty by popular and divine sanction.
preamble.remarkable: The praise poem for Simon (vv. 4-15) is the fullest picture of Maccabean idealism — a golden age where old men sit in the streets, farmers sow in peace, the land yields its produce, and 'each man sits under his vine and fig tree with none to make them afraid' (v. 12). This last phrase directly quotes Micah 4:4 and 1 Kings 4:25, presenting Simon's reign as the fulfillment of messianic prophecy.
preamble.friction: The great decree (vv. 27-49) establishes hereditary dynastic rule — something explicitly rejected in Samuel's warnings about monarchy (1 Samuel 8:10-18). The clause 'until a trustworthy prophet should arise' (v. 41) again acknowledges the absence of prophecy and limits Hasmonean authority in principle, even while granting it vast scope in practice.
preamble.connections: The 'vine and fig tree' imagery (v. 12) connects to Micah 4:4, Zechariah 3:10, and 1 Kings 4:25 — messianic peace language. The decree inscribed on bronze tablets (v. 48) echoes the Roman treaty (8:22). The conditional authority 'until a trustworthy prophet arise' connects to the unanswered question of the altar stones (4:46).

verses.text_latin: anno centesimo septuagesimo secundo congregavit rex Demetrius exercitus suos et abiit in Mediam ad contrahenda sibi auxilia ut expugnaret Tryphonem
verses.rendering: In the one hundred and seventy-second year, King Demetrius gathered his armies and marched into Media to secure reinforcements for his war against Trypho.

verses.text_latin: et audivit Arsaces rex Persidis et Mediae quia intravit Demetrius fines suos et misit unum de principibus suis ut conprehenderet eum vivum et adduceret eum
verses.rendering: When Arsaces, king of Persia and Media, heard that Demetrius had entered his territory, he sent one of his generals to take him alive.

key_terms.note: Mithridates I of Parthia (using the dynasty name Arsaces); his capture of Demetrius II removed the last effective Seleucid king from the scene

verses.text_latin: et abiit et percussit castra Demetrii et conprehendit eum et adduxit eum ad Arsacen et posuit eum in custodiam
verses.rendering: He went and defeated the army of Demetrius, captured him, and brought him to Arsaces, who put him in prison.

verses.text_latin: et siluit terra Iuda omnibus diebus Simonis et quaesivit bona genti suae et placuit illis potestas eius et gloria eius omnibus diebus
verses.rendering: The land of Judah was at rest all the days of Simon. He sought the good of his nation, and his authority and his glory pleased them all his days.
translator_notes: The praise poem begins here (vv. 4-15) — a carefully constructed portrait of the ideal ruler.

verses.text_latin: et cum omni gloria sua accepit Ioppen et fecit eam portum et fecit introitum in insulis maris
verses.rendering: In all his glory, he took Joppa for a harbor and made it a gateway to the islands of the sea.

verses.text_latin: et dilatavit fines gentis suae et obtinuit regionem
verses.rendering: He enlarged the borders of his nation and gained control of the countryside.

verses.text_latin: et congregavit captivitatem multam et dominatus est Gazarae et Bethsurae et arci et abstulit inmunditias ex ea et non erat qui resisteret ei
verses.rendering: He gathered a great number of captives. He gained mastery over Gezer, Beth-zur, and the citadel, removing their uncleanness. No one could resist him.

verses.text_latin: et unusquisque colebat terram suam cum pace et terra Iuda dabat fructus suos et ligna camporum fructum suum
verses.rendering: Each man tilled his land in peace. The land of Judah yielded its produce, and the trees of the field their fruit.

verses.text_latin: seniores in plateis sedebant omnes et de bonis terrae tractabant et iuvenes induebant se gloriam et stolas belli
verses.rendering: The elders sat in the streets; all spoke of the good of the land, and the young men clothed themselves in glory and in the garments of war.

verses.text_latin: civitatibus tribuebat alimenta et constituebat eas ut essent vasa munitionis quoadusque nominatum est nomen gloriae eius usque ad extremum terrae
verses.rendering: He supplied the cities with provisions and equipped them as fortresses, until his glorious name was renowned to the ends of the earth.

verses.text_latin: fecit pacem super terram et laetatus est Israhel laetitia magna
verses.rendering: He made peace upon the land, and Israel rejoiced with great gladness.

verses.text_latin: et sedit unusquisque sub vite sua et sub ficulnea sua et non erat qui eos terreret
verses.rendering: Each man sat under his vine and his fig tree, and there was none to make them afraid.
translator_notes: This verse directly quotes the messianic peace vision of Micah 4:4 and echoes Solomon's golden age (1 Kings 4:25). It is the highest praise the author can bestow — Simon's reign fulfills prophetic hope.

key_terms.latin: sub vite sua et sub ficulnea sua
key_terms.rendered_as: under his vine and his fig tree
key_terms.note: Micah 4:4, 1 Kings 4:25, Zechariah 3:10 — the quintessential image of messianic peace; Simon's reign presented as prophetic fulfillment

verses.text_latin: non erat qui eos expugnaret super terram reges contriti sunt in diebus illis
verses.rendering: No one was left to attack them in the land. The kings had been crushed in those days.

verses.text_latin: et confirmavit omnes humiles populi sui et legem exquisivit et abstulit omnem iniquum et malum
verses.rendering: He strengthened all the humble of his people. He sought out the Law and removed every lawless and wicked person.

verses.text_latin: sancta glorificavit et multiplicavit vasa sanctorum
verses.rendering: He made the sanctuary glorious and multiplied its sacred vessels.

verses.text_latin: et auditum est Romae quia defunctus est Ionathas et usque in Spartan et contristati sunt valde
verses.rendering: When word reached Rome — and Sparta as well — that Jonathan had died, they were deeply grieved.

verses.text_latin: ut audierunt autem quod Simon frater eius factus esset summus sacerdos loco eius et ipse obtineret omnem regionem et civitates in ea
verses.rendering: But when they heard that his brother Simon had become high priest in his place and controlled the whole region and its cities,

verses.text_latin: scripserunt ad eum in tabulis aereis ut renovarent amicitias et societatem quam fecerant cum Iuda et cum Ionatha fratribus eius
verses.rendering: they wrote to him on bronze tablets to renew the friendship and alliance they had established with his brothers Judas and Jonathan.

verses.text_latin: et lectae sunt in conspectu ecclesiae in Hierusalem
verses.rendering: These were read out before the assembly in Jerusalem.

verses.text_latin: et hoc est exemplum epistularum quas Spartiatae miserunt
verses.rendering: This is a copy of the letter the Spartans sent:

verses.text_latin: Spartianorum principes et civitates Simoni sacerdoti magno et senioribus et sacerdotibus et reliquo populo Iudaeorum fratribus salutem
verses.rendering: 'The rulers and citizens of the Spartans, to Simon the great high priest, the elders, the priests, and the rest of the people of the Jews, our brothers — greetings!'

verses.text_latin: legati qui missi sunt ad populum nostrum nuntiaverunt nobis de vestra gloria et honore et laetitia et gavisi sumus in introitu eorum
verses.rendering: 'The envoys sent to our people reported to us your glory, honor, and prosperity, and we rejoiced at their coming.'

verses.text_latin: et descripsimus quae ab eis erant dicta in conciliis populi sic Numenius Antiochi et Antipater Iasonis legati Iudaeorum venerunt ad nos renovantes nobiscum amicitiam
verses.rendering: 'We recorded their statements in the public records as follows: Numenius son of Antiochus and Antipater son of Jason, envoys of the Jews, came to us to renew their friendship with us.'

verses.text_latin: et placuit populo excipere viros gloriose et ponere exemplum sermonum eorum in segregatis populi libris ut sit in memoriam populo Spartiatarum exemplum autem horum scripsimus Simoni sacerdoti magno
verses.rendering: 'The people resolved to receive the men with honor and to place a copy of their words in the public archives, to serve as a memorial for the people of the Spartans. A copy of this has been sent to Simon the great high priest.'

verses.text_latin: post haec misit Simon Numenium Romam habentem clipeum aureum magnum pondo minarum mille ad statuendam cum eis societatem
verses.rendering: After this, Simon sent Numenius to Rome with a great golden shield weighing a thousand minas, to confirm the alliance with them.
translator_notes: A thousand-mina gold shield — an enormously valuable diplomatic gift, demonstrating the wealth and confidence of Simon's independent state.

key_terms.note: Diplomatic gift of extraordinary value — a statement of Judean wealth and sovereignty

verses.text_latin: cum autem audisset populus sermones istos dixerunt quam gratiam reddemus Simoni et filiis eius
verses.rendering: When the people heard these things, they said: 'How shall we repay Simon and his sons?'

verses.text_latin: restituit enim ipse et fratres eius et domus patris eius et expugnaverunt inimicos Israhel ab eis et statuerunt ei libertatem et scripserunt in tabulis aereis et posuerunt in titulis in monte Sion
verses.rendering: 'For he, his brothers, and his father's house have stood firm. They fought and repelled the enemies of Israel, and they established its freedom.' They inscribed this on bronze tablets and set it up on pillars on Mount Zion.

verses.text_latin: et hoc est exemplum scripturae octava decima die mensis Elul anno centesimo septuagesimo secundo anno tertio sub Simone sacerdote magno in Asaramel
verses.rendering: This is a copy of the inscription: 'On the eighteenth day of Elul, in the one hundred and seventy-second year — which is the third year of Simon the great high priest — in Asaramel,
translator_notes: 'Asaramel' is debated — possibly a place name, or a Hebrew phrase meaning 'in the court of the people of God.'

key_terms.note: Possibly Hebrew asar am El — 'court of the people of God'; the assembly where the decree was promulgated

verses.text_latin: in conventu magno sacerdotum et populi et principum gentis et seniorum regionis nota facta sunt nobis
verses.rendering: in a great assembly of the priests, the people, the rulers of the nation, and the elders of the country, the following was proclaimed to us:'

verses.text_latin: quoniam frequenter facta sunt proelia in regione nostra Simon autem Matthathiae filius ex filiis Iarib et fratres eius dederunt se periculo et restiterunt adversariis gentis suae ut starent sancta ipsorum et lex et gloria magna glorificaverunt gentem suam
verses.rendering: 'Since there have been many wars in our land, Simon son of Mattathias, of the sons of Joarib, and his brothers risked their lives and resisted the enemies of their nation, so that their sanctuary and the Law might be preserved. They brought great glory to their nation.'

verses.text_latin: et congregavit Ionathas gentem suam et factus est illis sacerdos magnus et adpositus est ad populum suum
verses.rendering: 'Jonathan rallied his nation and became their high priest, and then was gathered to his people.'

verses.text_latin: et voluerunt inimici eorum calcare et adterere regionem ipsorum et extendere manus in sancta eorum
verses.rendering: 'Their enemies sought to trample and destroy their land and to lay hands on their sanctuary.'

verses.text_latin: tunc restitit Simon et pugnavit pro gente sua et erogavit pecunias multas et armavit viros virtutis gentis suae et dedit illis stipendia
verses.rendering: 'Then Simon arose and fought for his nation. He spent much of his own money to arm the brave men of his nation and gave them pay.'

verses.text_latin: et munivit civitates Iudaeae et Bethsuram quae erat in finibus Iudaeae ubi erant arma hostium antea et posuit illic praesidium viros Iudaeos
verses.rendering: 'He fortified the cities of Judea, and Beth-zur on the borders of Judea where the enemy had formerly stored their weapons. He stationed a Jewish garrison there.'

verses.text_latin: et Ioppen munivit quae erat ad mare et Gazaram quae est in finibus Azoti in qua hostes antea habitabant et collocavit illic Iudaeos et quaecumque apta erant ad correptionem eorum posuit in eis
verses.rendering: 'He fortified Joppa by the sea and Gezer on the border of Azotus, where the enemy had formerly dwelt. He settled Jews there and provided them with everything needed for their restoration.'

verses.text_latin: et vidit populus actum Simonis et gloriam quam cogitabat facere genti suae et posuerunt eum ducem suum et principem sacerdotum eo quod ipse fecerat haec omnia et iustitiam et fidem quam conservavit genti suae et exquisivit omni modo exaltare populum suum
verses.rendering: 'The people saw Simon's deeds and the glory he planned to bring to his nation, and they made him their leader and high priest, because he had done all these things, and because of the justice and the faithfulness he maintained toward his nation, and because he sought in every way to exalt his people.'

verses.text_latin: et in diebus eius prosperatum est in manibus eius ut tollerentur gentes de regione ipsorum et qui in civitate David erant in Hierusalem in arce de qua procedebant et contaminabant omnia quae in circuitu sanctificationis sunt et inferebant plagam magnam castitati
verses.rendering: 'In his days, the work prospered in his hands so that the Gentiles were removed from their territory, and those in the City of David in Jerusalem in the citadel — from which they used to sally forth and defile everything around the sanctuary, inflicting great damage on its holiness.'

verses.text_latin: et collocavit in ea viros Iudaeos et munivit eam ad tutamentum regionis et civitatis et exaltavit muros Hierusalem
verses.rendering: 'He settled Jewish men in it and fortified it for the security of the region and the city, and he raised the walls of Jerusalem.'

verses.text_latin: et rex Demetrius statuit illi summum sacerdotium
verses.rendering: 'King Demetrius confirmed him in the high priesthood.'

verses.text_latin: secundum haec constituit eum amicum suum et glorificavit eum gloria magna
verses.rendering: 'In accordance with these things, he made him one of his Friends and honored him with great glory.'

verses.text_latin: audivit enim quod appellati sunt Iudaei a Romanis amici et socii et fratres et quia susceperunt legatos Simonis gloriose
verses.rendering: 'For he had heard that the Jews were called by the Romans friends and allies and brothers, and that they had received Simon's envoys with honor.'

verses.text_latin: et quia Iudaei et sacerdotes eorum consenserunt ut esset dux eorum et summus sacerdos in aeternum donec surgat propheta fidelis
verses.rendering: 'The Jews and their priests resolved that Simon should be their leader and high priest forever, until a trustworthy prophet should arise.'
translator_notes: 'Donec surgat propheta fidelis' — 'until a trustworthy prophet should arise' — the critical qualifier. Hasmonean authority is explicitly provisional, awaiting prophetic confirmation that never came during the dynasty.

key_terms.rendered_as: until a trustworthy prophet should arise
key_terms.note: The key limitation on Hasmonean authority — it is provisional pending prophetic confirmation; connects to 4:46 and anticipates messianic expectation

verses.text_latin: et ut esset super eos dux et ut cura esset illi de sanctis constituere praepositos super opera eorum et super regionem et super arma et super praesidia
verses.rendering: 'He shall be their governor, with responsibility for the sanctuary, to appoint overseers for its works, for the country, for the weapons, and for the fortresses.'

verses.text_latin: et cura sit illi de sanctis et ut audiatur ab omnibus et scribantur in nomine eius omnes conscriptiones in regione et ut operiatur purpura et auro
verses.rendering: 'He shall have charge of the sanctuary. He shall be obeyed by all. All contracts in the country shall be written in his name. He shall be clothed in purple and gold.'

verses.text_latin: et non liceat ulli ex populo et ex sacerdotibus irritum facere aliquid horum et contradicere his quae ab eo dicuntur aut convocare conventum in regione sine ipso et vestiri purpura et uti fibula aurea
verses.rendering: 'No one among the people or the priests shall be permitted to annul any of these decisions, to contradict his pronouncements, to convene an assembly in the country without his consent, to wear purple, or to use a golden buckle.'

verses.text_latin: qui autem fecerit extra haec aut irritum fecerit aliquid horum reus erit
verses.rendering: 'Whoever acts contrary to these provisions or annuls any of them shall be held guilty.'

verses.text_latin: et complacuit omni populo statuere Simoni et facere secundum verba ista
verses.rendering: 'All the people agreed to grant Simon authority to act according to these terms.'

verses.text_latin: et suscepit Simon et placuit ut fungatur summo sacerdotio et sit dux et ethnarca Iudaeorum et sacerdotum et praesit omnibus
verses.rendering: Simon accepted and was pleased to serve as high priest and to be commander and ethnarch of the Jews and the priests, and to preside over all.

key_terms.note: Ruler of the nation — a title below king but above governor; the formal designation of Hasmonean political authority

verses.text_latin: et scripturam istam dixerunt ponere in tabulis aereis et statuere eas in peribolo sanctorum in loco celebri
verses.rendering: They ordered this decree to be inscribed on bronze tablets and set up in a conspicuous place in the precinct of the sanctuary.
translator_notes: The bronze tablets in the Temple precinct — a permanent public monument enshrining the Hasmonean dynasty in Israel's most sacred space.

verses.text_latin: exemplum autem eorum ponere in aerario ut habeat Simon et filii eius
verses.rendering: A copy was also to be deposited in the treasury, to be held by Simon and his sons.
